Consider the curve given by $$x^2 + xy + y^2 = 27$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_{-1}^{2} \left(3x^{2} + 2x - 3\right)dx$$?

options.why: This is F(b) only; subtract F(a) as well.
This adds F(a) instead of subtracting it.
Correct. An antiderivative is $$F(x) = x^{3} + x^{2} - 3x$$; $$F(2) - F(-1) = 3$$.
This subtracts values of the integrand instead of an antiderivative.

questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $$\int_{-1}^{2} f(x)\,dx = F(2) - F(-1)$$ with $$F(x) = x^{3} + x^{2} - 3x$$. That is $$6 - (3) = 3$$.

questions.stem: Let $$C(x)$$ be the cost, in dollars, of producing x items. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $$C'(2) = 1$$?

options.text: The average rate of change of the cost over the first 2 items is 1 dollars per item.
options.why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at one input, not an average over an interval.

options.text: The cost when 2 items have been produced is 1.
options.why: This describes $$C(2)$$, the value of the function, not its rate of change.

options.text: The cost changes by 1 over the first 2 items.
options.why: This describes a total change over an interval, which is an integral of the rate, not the derivative at one point.

options.text: The cost is increasing at a rate of 1 dollars per item when 2 items have been produced.
options.why: Correct. A derivative at a point is an instantaneous rate of change, with units of output per unit of input.

questions.explanation: $$C'(2)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$C$$ when 2 items have been produced. Its sign (positive) says the cost is increasing, and its units are dollars per item.

questions.stem: What is the average value of $$f(x) = -6x^{2} + 6$$ on the interval $$[0, 2]$$?

options.why: This is the average rate of change of f, not the average value.
Correct. $$\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2} f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(-4\right)$$.
This is the integral; divide by the length of the interval.
This averages the endpoint values, which only works for linear functions.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to -3} \frac{x^{2} + 8x + 15}{x + 3}$$?

options.why: Correct. The numerator factors as $$(x + 3)(x + 5)$$. Cancel $$x + 3$$ and substitute: $$-3 - (-5) = 2$$.
This adds the roots. After cancelling, the expression is $$x + 5$$, which approaches $$2$$.
The expression is undefined at the point, but its outputs nearby approach a single number, so the limit exists.
Substituting gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, an indeterminate form, not the value 0.

questions.explanation: Direct substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, so factor: $$x^{2} + 8x + 15 = (x + 3)(x + 5)$$. For $$x \neq -3$$ the expression equals $$x + 5$$, so the limit is $$-3 - (-5) = 2$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of $$f(x) = x^{2} + 5x + 4$$ at $$x = 2$$?

This uses the function value $$18$$ as the slope.
This swaps the x- and y-coordinates of the point of tangency.
Correct. The point is $$(2, 18)$$ and the slope is $$f'(2) = 9$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \frac{x^{2} + 3x - 4}{x^{2} - 5x + 4}$$. Which of the following lists every vertical asymptote of the graph of $$f$$?

options.why: $$x = 1$$ is a hole, because its factor cancels.
Correct. The factor $$x - 1$$ cancels, leaving a hole at $$x = 1$$. Only $$x = 4$$ makes the simplified denominator zero.
At $$x = 1$$ the numerator is also zero; the common factor cancels, giving a removable discontinuity (a hole), not an asymptote.
$$x = -4$$ is a zero of the numerator, so it is an x-intercept, not an asymptote.

questions.explanation: Factor: $$f(x) = \frac{(x - 1)(x + 4)}{(x - 1)(x - 4)}$$. The common factor gives a hole at $$x = 1$$; near $$x = 4$$ the denominator approaches 0 while the numerator does not, so $$x = 4$$ is the only vertical asymptote.

questions.stem: The edge length of a cube is increasing at a constant rate of 5 centimeters per second. At the instant when the edge length is 7 centimeters, what is the rate of change of the volume?

questions.explanation: $$\frac{dV}{dt} = 3s^2\frac{ds}{dt}$$. Substitute the dimension $$7$$ and its rate $$5$$ to get $$735$$ (cubic or square centimeters per second).

questions.explanation: $$\int \frac{dx}{x + 3} = \ln|x + 3| + C$$, so the integral is $$\ln\frac{15}{3} = \ln 5$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{2} - 2x$$. What value of $$c$$ satisfies the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem for $$f$$ on the interval $$[-1, 5]$$?

options.why: Correct. The average rate of change is $$\frac{f(5) - f(-1)}{6} = 2$$, and $$f'(c) = 2c - 2 = 2$$ gives $$c = 2$$.
The MVT guarantees a point strictly inside the interval, and this endpoint doesn't satisfy the equation.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} -2x + 6 & x < 1 \\ -4x - 4 & x \geq 1 \end{cases}$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x)$$?

options.why: One-sided limits can exist even when the two-sided limit does not.

questions.explanation: The left-hand limit uses the piece for $$x < 1$$: $$-2(1) + 6 = 4$$.

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = x^{3} - 27x + 5$$ on the closed interval $$[-5, 5]$$?

options.why: Correct. Compare $$f$$ at the critical points $$x = \pm 3$$ and the endpoints: the largest value is $$59$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{1} x\left(x^2 + 1\right)dx$$?

options.why: This evaluates only at the upper limit.
After substituting, the limits must change to u-values (from c to 1 + c), not stay 0 to 1.
This forgets the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$ from $$du = 2x\,dx$$.
Correct. With $$u = x^2 + 1$$, $$du = 2x\,dx$$, the integral is $$\frac{1}{2}\int_{1}^{2} u\,du$$.
The antiderivative of $$2x$$ is $$\frac{2}{2}x^2$$.
You cannot integrate a quotient by integrating the top and bottom separately.
Correct. Divide first: $$\frac{2x^{2} - 4}{x} = 2x + \frac{-4}{x}$$.

questions.explanation: $$\int \left(2x + \frac{-4}{x}\right)dx = x^2 - 4\ln|x| + C$$.

questions.stem: What is the area of the region enclosed by the curves $$x = y^2$$ and $$x = 4y$$?

options.why: This is the area under the parabola alone.
Correct. $$\int_0^{4} (4y - y^2)\,dy$$: right curve minus left curve.
An area is never negative; this subtracts the curves in the wrong order.
This is the area under the line alone.

questions.explanation: The curves meet at $$0$$ and $$4$$. Area $$= \int_0^{4} (4u - u^2)\,du = \frac{4u^2}{2} - \frac{u^3}{3}\Big|_0^{4} = \frac{32}{3}$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3} + h\right) - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)}{h}$$?

questions.stem: If $$f(x) = \arcsin\left(\frac{x}{13}\right)$$, what is $$f'(5)$$?

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = 2x^{3} - 24x^{2} + 72x$$. At what value of $$x$$ does $$f$$ have a relative minimum?

options.why: Correct. $$f'(x) = 6(x - 2)(x - 6)$$ changes from negative to positive at $$x = 6$$.

This is where f″ = 0 (the inflection point), not a critical point.

questions.explanation: $$f'(x) = 6x^2 - 48x + 72 = 6(x - 2)(x - 6)$$. Testing signs: $$f'$$ is positive left of $$2$$, negative between $$2$$ and $$6$$, positive right of $$6$$. So there is a relative maximum at $$2$$ and a relative minimum at $$6$$.

questions.stem: A 10-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 2 feet per second. How fast is the top of the ladder moving, in feet per second, when the bottom is 6 feet from the wall?

options.why: The top slides down, so its rate is negative.
Correct. $$x^2 + y^2 = 100$$ gives $$x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$$. With $$x = 6$$, $$y = 8$$, $$\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{6(2)}{8}$$.
This swaps the roles of x and y.
The two ends do not move at the same speed; their rates depend on the position.

questions.explanation: Let $$x$$ be the distance from the wall and $$y$$ the height. $$2x x' + 2y y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x x'}{y} = -\frac{6 \cdot 2}{8} = -\frac{3}{2}$$ feet per second (the top is moving down).

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 18 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{3}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 73 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 8$$?

questions.explanation: Amount = initial amount + accumulated change = $$73 + \int_0^{8} R(t)\,dt \approx 73 + 196.245 = 269.245$$ cubic feet.

questions.stem: A farmer has 168 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the largest possible area of the field, in square meters?

options.why: Correct. With width $$x$$ perpendicular to the river, $$A = x(168 - 2x)$$, maximized at $$x = 42$$.
This makes all three fenced sides equal, which is not optimal.
This doesn't account for the two equal sides perpendicular to the river.
This fences all four sides (a square), but the river side needs no fence.

questions.explanation: $$A(x) = x(168 - 2x)$$, $$A'(x) = 168 - 4x = 0$$ at $$x = 42$$, and $$A'' = -4 < 0$$, so this is a maximum. The dimensions are $$42$$ by $$84$$, with area $$3528$$.

questions.stem: The temperature of a room, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modeled by $$H(t) = 73 + 16\sin\left(\frac{t}{4}\right)e^{-t/20}$$, where $$t$$ is measured in hours. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the temperature at $$t = 9$$, in degrees Fahrenheit per hour?

questions.stem: The function $$g$$ is defined by $$g(x) = \frac{\sin(5x)}{e^{6x} - 1}$$ for $$x \neq 0$$. For what value of $$g(0)$$ is $$g$$ continuous at $$x = 0$$?

questions.explanation: For continuity, $$g(0)$$ must equal $$\lim_{x \to 0} g(x)$$. Near 0, $$\sin(5x) \approx 5x$$ and $$e^{6x} - 1 \approx 6x$$, so the limit is $$\frac{5}{6} \approx 0.833$$. A table of values near 0 confirms it.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{3} + 2x + e^{x/2}$$, and let $$g$$ be the inverse of $$f$$. What is the value of $$g'(6)$$?
